framework.name: CSA CCM
framework.description: Cloud Security Alliance Cloud Controls Matrix v4.1.1: 207 control specifications in 17 domains for cloud service providers and customers. Requirement text is paraphrased; the control IDs and titles follow the CCM.

supplementaryControls.title: Tenant segmentation and isolation
supplementaryControls.description: Design and operate the service so each customer's (tenant's) access and data are segmented and segregated from other tenants, with cross-tenant access restricted and monitored
supplementaryControls.question: Is each customer's environment and data separated from other customers' in the service, with any cross-tenant access restricted and monitored?
supplementaryControls.intent: In shared platforms a flaw in tenant isolation exposes one customer's data to another, which network segregation alone does not prevent.
examples: Per-tenant data partitioning or encryption keys
Isolation tests in the release process

supplementaryControls.title: Shared security responsibility model
supplementaryControls.description: Document which party (provider, customer, subprocessor) owns each security control for the service, give customers guidance on it, and review it at planned intervals
supplementaryControls.question: Is the split of security responsibilities between us, our customers and our suppliers documented for this service, shared with customers and reviewed?
supplementaryControls.intent: Cloud customers and providers each operate part of the controls; unclear ownership leaves controls that nobody runs.
examples: Shared responsibility matrix published to customers
Control ownership recorded for each cloud supplier

supplementaryControls.title: Customer-managed encryption keys
supplementaryControls.description: Offer customers the ability to manage the encryption keys that protect their own data in the service
supplementaryControls.question: Can customers manage (supply, rotate or revoke) the encryption keys that protect their data in this service?
supplementaryControls.intent: Customers who hold their own keys keep control of access to their data, even when the provider hosts it.
examples: Integration with the customer's key management service

supplementaryControls.title: Customer data portability and exit
supplementaryControls.description: Give customers programmatic access to retrieve their data and agree in contract how data is returned, retained and deleted when the service ends
supplementaryControls.question: Can customers retrieve their data programmatically, and do the agreements state the format, retention period, scope and deletion on termination?
supplementaryControls.intent: Customers need to move data in and out of the service and leave it without losing control of their data.
examples: Export API or bulk export in an open format
Contract clause on data return and deletion after termination

supplementaryControls.title: Data location transparency
supplementaryControls.description: Record and keep current the physical locations where customer data is stored, processed and backed up
supplementaryControls.question: Are the physical locations where data of this service is stored, processed and backed up documented and kept up to date?
supplementaryControls.intent: Location determines which laws and authorities apply to the data, so customers and the organisation need to know where it is.
examples: Register of regions and sites used
Change notice to customers when a region changes

supplementaryControls.title: Customer authorisation of provider access and changes
supplementaryControls.description: Limit provider changes that directly affect a customer's environment to explicitly authorised requests, and involve the customer in granting agreed high-risk privileged access to it
supplementaryControls.question: Are changes to a customer's environment and provider staff's high-risk privileged access to it limited to what the customer has authorised?
supplementaryControls.intent: A provider can reach into customer environments; customers need a say over when and how that happens.
examples: Contract clause limiting changes to authorised requests
Customer approval step for privileged support access
Access records available to the customer

requirements.title: Audit and Assurance Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Audit and assurance should be governed by approved and communicated policies, procedures and standards, revisited yearly or after a material change.

mappings.rationale: Covers independent review of security, but does not require a dedicated audit and assurance policy

requirements.title: Independent Assessments
requirements.text: Have independent parties carry out audit and assurance assessments against recognised standards, at least once a year.

requirements.title: Risk Based Planning Assessment
requirements.text: Plan independent assessments on the basis of risk, and also run them when major changes or newly emerging risks call for it.

mappings.rationale: Reviews are planned at intervals, but triggering them by emerging risks is not explicit

requirements.title: Requirements Compliance
requirements.text: Confirm that the audit scope accounts for every applicable standard, law, contractual duty and statutory rule.

mappings.rationale: Checks compliance with policies and standards; legal and contractual audit scope is not explicit
Identifies legal and contractual requirements but does not require verifying audit coverage of them

requirements.title: Audit Management Process
requirements.text: An audit management process aligned with auditing standards should cover audit planning, risk analysis, control assessment, conclusions, remediation schedules and report production, and include a look back at earlier reports and evidence.

requirements.title: Remediation
requirements.text: Keep a risk-driven corrective action plan for audit findings, and report remediation progress to stakeholders on a regular basis.

mappings.rationale: Management review reports on audit results, but stakeholder reporting of remediation status is not explicit

requirements.title: Application and Interface Security Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Application security should be governed by approved policies and procedures that are communicated and put into practice, and revisited yearly or after a material change.

mappings.rationale: Covers rules for secure development, not a general application security policy
Covers application security requirements, not the surrounding policy and review cycle

requirements.title: Application Security Baseline Requirements
requirements.text: Define and keep up to date the baseline security requirements that applications must meet.

requirements.title: Application Security Metrics
requirements.text: Set technical and operational application security metrics that tie to business goals, security needs and compliance duties, and put them into use.

mappings.rationale: Requires measuring ISMS performance generally, not application-specific metrics

requirements.title: Secure Application Development Lifecycle
requirements.text: Run a secure software development lifecycle spanning requirements, planning, design, build, test, deployment and operation of applications.

requirements.title: Application Security Testing
requirements.text: Adopt an application testing strategy, with acceptance criteria for new systems, upgrades and releases, that gives security assurance without blocking delivery. Automate it where this is practical.

requirements.title: Secure Application Deployment
requirements.text: Provide standardised, compliant and secure ways to deploy applications, automating them wherever possible.

mappings.rationale: Change control covers deployments, but a standardised and automated secure deployment capability is not required
Covers controlled installation of software, not deployment strategy or automation

requirements.title: Application Vulnerability Remediation
requirements.text: Operate a process for fixing application security vulnerabilities, with automated fixing where it can be done.

requirements.title: API Security
requirements.text: Put processes, procedures and technical safeguards in place to secure APIs, and revisit them for improvement every year or after significant change.

mappings.rationale: Covers security of application services on public networks, but APIs are not addressed explicitly
Covers network and service security generally, not API-specific safeguards

requirements.section: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
requirements.title: Business Continuity Management Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Business continuity and operational resilience should be governed by approved and communicated policies and procedures, revisited yearly or after a material change.

mappings.rationale: Covers ICT readiness for continuity, not an overall business continuity policy
Covers security during disruption, not a business continuity management policy

requirements.section: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
requirements.title: Risk Assessment and Impact Analysis
requirements.text: Assess how disruptions and risks would affect the business, and use the result as criteria for continuity and resilience strategies. Refresh the assessment yearly or after significant change.

mappings.rationale: ICT readiness is based on continuity objectives, but a formal impact analysis and its annual refresh are not explicit
Addresses security during disruption, not the impact analysis

requirements.section: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
requirements.title: Business Continuity Strategy
requirements.text: Define strategies that lessen the effect of business disruptions and improve the ability to withstand and recover from them.

requirements.section: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
requirements.title: Business Continuity Planning
requirements.text: Maintain an approved and communicated business continuity plan that follows from the chosen resilience strategies and capabilities.

mappings.rationale: Covers security during disruption, not the whole business continuity plan

requirements.section: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
requirements.title: Documentation
requirements.text: Gather the documentation, from inside and outside the organisation, that supports continuity and resilience plans, make it available to authorised stakeholders and review it yearly or after significant change.

mappings.rationale: Plans must be documented, but collecting external documentation and the review cycle are not explicit
Operating procedures are documented and available, but continuity documentation is not specifically addressed

requirements.section: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
requirements.title: Business Continuity Exercises
requirements.text: Exercise and test continuity and resilience plans yearly or after significant change.

requirements.section: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
requirements.title: Communication
requirements.text: Open and sustain lines of communication to all relevant stakeholders while continuity and resilience procedures are carried out.

mappings.rationale: Covers security during disruption, but stakeholder communication channels are not explicit

requirements.section: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
requirements.title: Backup
requirements.text: Back up regularly, safeguard the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the backups, and prove that data can be restored from them.

requirements.section: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
requirements.title: Disaster Response Plan
requirements.text: Maintain an approved disaster response plan for recovering from natural and human-made disasters, updated yearly or after significant change.

mappings.rationale: Covers ICT continuity, but disaster-specific response planning is not explicit
Covers protection against physical and environmental threats, not disaster recovery planning

requirements.section: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
requirements.title: Response Plan Exercise
requirements.text: Rehearse the disaster response plan each year or after significant change, involving local emergency authorities where possible.

mappings.rationale: ICT readiness must be tested, but the disaster plan exercise and authority participation are not explicit
Covers contact with authorities, not joint exercises

requirements.section: Business Continuity Management and Operational Resilience
requirements.title: Equipment Redundancy
requirements.text: Back business-critical equipment with redundant units, both on site and geographically separated by a sensible distance, following industry norms.

mappings.rationale: Requires redundancy of processing facilities, but not geographic dispersion

requirements.title: Change Management Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Policies and procedures governing the risk of changing assets the organisation owns, controls or uses should be approved, communicated and revisited yearly or after a material change.

requirements.title: Quality Testing
requirements.text: Operate a defined process for change control, approval and testing that rests on baselines, test steps and release standards.

mappings.rationale: Covers configuration baselines, not release standards and testing

requirements.title: Change Management Technology
requirements.text: Use a change management procedure to control the risks of changes to assets that the organisation owns, controls or uses.

requirements.title: Unauthorized Change Protection
requirements.text: Enforce a procedure that authorises adding, removing, updating and managing organisational assets.

mappings.rationale: Covers control of software installation only, not all asset changes

requirements.title: Change Agreements
requirements.text: Contractually limit changes that directly affect customer-owned environments (tenants) to requests the customer has explicitly authorised within agreed service levels.

mappings.rationale: Covers security terms in supplier agreements, not limiting provider changes to authorised requests

requirements.title: Change Management Baseline
requirements.text: Define and apply change and configuration baselines for all authorised changes to organisational assets, reviewing them yearly or after significant change.

requirements.title: Detection of Baseline Deviation
requirements.text: Detect changes that depart from the established baseline and notify the responsible people in advance of harm.

mappings.rationale: Configurations must be monitored, but proactive notification of deviations is not explicit
Covers monitoring for anomalous behaviour, not configuration drift

requirements.title: Exception Management
requirements.text: Handle exceptions, emergencies included, to the change and configuration process through a defined procedure that is in line with the policy exception process.

mappings.rationale: Change management is covered, but an exception and emergency change procedure is not explicit
Covers compliance with policies, not exceptions to them

requirements.title: Change Restoration
requirements.text: Define a process that reverts changes to the last known good state when errors or security concerns arise.

mappings.rationale: Change control is covered, but rollback to a known good state is not required

requirements.title: Encryption and Key Management Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Cryptography, encryption and key management should be governed by an approved policy and procedure set that is communicated to staff and revisited yearly or after a material change.

requirements.title: CEK Roles and Responsibilities
requirements.text: Assign roles and responsibilities for cryptography, encryption and key management.

mappings.rationale: Roles must be defined generally, but not cryptography-specific ones
Covers key management rules but not explicit role assignment

requirements.title: Data Protection
requirements.text: Protect data while stored, in transit and, where relevant, in use, using cryptographic libraries certified to recognised standards.

mappings.rationale: Covers effective use of cryptography, but certified libraries and protection of data in use are not explicit

requirements.title: Encryption Algorithm
requirements.text: Pick industry-standard encryption algorithms suited to how the data is classified and what risks surround it.

requirements.title: Encryption Change Management
requirements.text: Changes to cryptographic, encryption and key management technology, whether prompted inside or outside the organisation, need a standard routine for review, approval, rollout and communication.

mappings.rationale: Generic change management; cryptography-specific change handling is not explicit
Covers cryptography rules but not their change process

requirements.title: Encryption Change Cost Benefit Analysis
requirements.text: Before adopting changes to cryptographic systems and their policies, weigh the downstream effects, remaining risk, cost and benefit.

mappings.rationale: Risk assessment is covered generally, not cost-benefit analysis of cryptographic changes
Change management covers impact analysis but not cryptography-specific cost-benefit

requirements.title: Encryption Risk Management
requirements.text: Run a risk programme for encryption and key management covering assessment, treatment, context, monitoring and feedback.

mappings.rationale: Generic information security risk assessment, not a cryptography-specific programme
Covers cryptography rules but not a dedicated risk programme

requirements.title: Service Customer Key Management Capability
requirements.text: Providers must let their customers manage the encryption keys that protect the customers' own data.

requirements.title: Encryption and Key Management Audit
requirements.text: Subject encryption and key management systems, policies and processes to audit. The more risk a system carries, the more often (continuous is best, yearly the minimum), and also after any security event.

mappings.rationale: Independent review is covered generally, not risk-proportionate cryptography audits
Covers the cryptography rules but not auditing them

requirements.title: Key Generation
requirements.text: Keys must be generated with recognised cryptographic libraries, and the strength of the algorithm and the random number generator in use must be stated.

mappings.rationale: Key management is covered generally; key generation requirements are not explicit

requirements.title: Key Purpose
requirements.text: Provision secret and private keys for one purpose only.

mappings.rationale: Key management is covered generally; single-purpose keys are not explicit

requirements.title: Key Rotation
requirements.text: Rotate keys according to a calculated cryptoperiod that considers disclosure risk and legal and regulatory demands.

mappings.rationale: Key lifecycle is covered generally; rotation by cryptoperiod is not explicit

requirements.title: Key Revocation
requirements.text: Have a way to revoke and remove keys before their cryptoperiod ends, if a key is compromised or its holder leaves, respecting legal and regulatory duties.

mappings.rationale: Key lifecycle is covered generally; revocation is not explicit

requirements.title: Key Destruction
requirements.text: Securely destroy keys that are no longer needed, respecting legal and regulatory duties.

mappings.rationale: Key lifecycle is covered generally; key destruction is not explicit

requirements.title: Key Activation
requirements.text: Newly generated keys should stay in a pre-activated state until someone authorises their use, with attention to legal and regulatory obligations.

mappings.rationale: Key lifecycle is covered generally; the pre-activation state is not explicit

requirements.title: Key Suspension
requirements.text: Monitor, review and approve every move of a key into or out of suspension, respecting legal and regulatory duties.

mappings.rationale: Key lifecycle is covered generally; suspension handling is not explicit

requirements.title: Key Deactivation
requirements.text: Deactivate keys when they expire, respecting legal and regulatory duties.

mappings.rationale: Key lifecycle is covered generally; deactivation at expiry is not explicit

requirements.title: Key Archival
requirements.text: Archived keys belong in a secure repository where access follows least privilege, with legal and regulatory obligations in mind.

mappings.rationale: Key lifecycle is covered generally; archive handling is not explicit

requirements.title: Key Compromise
requirements.text: Once a key is compromised, allow it only for decrypting existing data and never again for encrypting, and only encrypt with it under controlled conditions, respecting legal and regulatory duties.

requirements.title: Key Recovery
requirements.text: Weigh the risk to operational continuity of losing the keys against the risk of exposing the keys and the data they protect, and set key recovery accordingly, respecting legal and regulatory duties.

mappings.rationale: Key lifecycle is covered generally; recovery risk trade-off is not explicit

requirements.title: Key Inventory Management
requirements.text: Have the key management system track and report all cryptographic material and each change of its status, respecting legal and regulatory duties.

mappings.rationale: Key lifecycle is covered generally; a key inventory is not explicit
Covers an inventory of assets, which may not include cryptographic keys

requirements.title: Physical and Environmental Security Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Physical and environmental security should be governed by approved and communicated policies and procedures, revisited yearly or after a material change.

mappings.rationale: Covers perimeters; a dedicated physical and environmental policy is not required
Covers environmental threats, not the policy framework

requirements.title: Off-Site Equipment Disposal Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Equipment used away from the organisation's premises needs approved disposal procedures; if it is not physically destroyed, data must be erased so it cannot be recovered. Revisit them yearly or after a material change.

mappings.rationale: Covers security of off-premises assets in general

requirements.title: Off-Site Transfer Authorization Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Approved procedures should govern moving hardware, software or data to another or off-site location, and each move needs written or cryptographically verifiable authorisation. Revisit them yearly or after a material change.

mappings.rationale: Covers off-premises assets, but authorised relocation is not explicit
Covers transport of storage media only

requirements.title: Secure Area Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Offices, rooms and other facilities need approved procedures that keep the working environment safe and secure; revisit them yearly or following a material change.

mappings.rationale: Covers working in secure areas but not the full policy

requirements.title: Secure Media Transportation Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Approved procedures should govern the secure transport of physical media; revisit them yearly or after a material change.

requirements.title: Assets Classification
requirements.text: Classify and document physical and logical assets, such as applications, by business risk, and revisit the classification yearly or after significant change.

mappings.rationale: Covers an inventory with owners; risk-based classification of assets is not explicit
Covers classification of information, not physical assets

requirements.title: Assets Cataloguing and Tracking
requirements.text: Catalogue and track the relevant physical and logical assets at all of the provider's sites in a secured system, and review the catalogue yearly or after significant change.

requirements.title: Controlled Physical Access Points
requirements.text: Design and put in place physical security perimeters that protect people, data and information systems.

requirements.title: Equipment Identification
requirements.text: Use the identity of equipment as a basis for authenticating its network connection.

requirements.title: Secure Area Authorization
requirements.text: Only people with authorisation may enter secure areas; every point of entry and exit is restricted, recorded and watched through physical access controls, and access records are kept for a period the organisation judges appropriate.

requirements.title: Surveillance System
requirements.text: Operate surveillance at the datacenter's outer perimeter and all entry and exit points to detect unauthorised attempts to get in or out.

requirements.title: Adverse Event Response Training
requirements.text: Train datacenter staff to handle adverse events safely, including unauthorised entry or exit attempts.

mappings.rationale: Covers awareness and training generally, not datacenter adverse event response

requirements.title: Cabling Security
requirements.text: Protect power and telecommunications cables against interception, interference and damage in all facilities, offices and rooms, in proportion to risk.

requirements.title: Environmental Systems
requirements.text: Run datacenter environmental controls that monitor, maintain and regularly test temperature and humidity within accepted industry ranges.

mappings.rationale: Covers environmental threats generally; temperature and humidity control is not explicit
Covers supporting utilities, which may include climate control

requirements.title: Secure Utilities
requirements.text: Secure, monitor, maintain and periodically test utility services so they stay effective.

requirements.title: Equipment Location
requirements.text: Avoid siting business-critical equipment where environmental hazards are likely.

requirements.title: Datacenter Metrics
requirements.text: Measure and report on datacenter security so that datacenter assets and services stay protected.

mappings.rationale: Requires measuring ISMS performance generally, not datacenter metrics

requirements.title: Datacenter Operations Resilience
requirements.text: Ensure datacenter operations continue without interruption through suitable processes, procedures and technical measures.

mappings.rationale: Covers ICT readiness for continuity, not datacenter operations specifically
Covers redundancy of processing facilities

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Security and Privacy Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Data should be prepared, classified, protected and handled over its whole lifecycle under approved and communicated policies and procedures that reflect applicable laws, standards and risk level; revisit them yearly or after a material change.

mappings.rationale: Covers classification of information, not the full data lifecycle policy
Covers privacy and PII protection, not all data types

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Secure Disposal
requirements.text: Dispose of data on storage media only with accepted methods that leave nothing recoverable by forensic means.

mappings.rationale: Covers deletion of information no longer required, without a forensic-unrecoverability standard

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Data Inventory
requirements.text: Create and keep an inventory of data, at least for sensitive, regulated and personal data, and review it yearly or after significant change.

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Data Classification
requirements.text: Classify data by its type, how critical it is and how sensitive it is.

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Data Flow Documentation
requirements.text: Document how data flows, showing what is processed, stored or transmitted and where, and review the documentation at set intervals, at least yearly.

mappings.rationale: Covers rules for information transfer, but data flow documentation is not required
Covers an inventory of information, not flow documentation

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Data Ownership and Stewardship
requirements.text: Record who owns and who stewards the relevant personal and sensitive data, and review this at least once a year.

mappings.rationale: Requires an owner for each asset, but not stewardship documentation or annual review
Covers privacy of PII, but not stewardship records

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Data Protection by Design and Default
requirements.text: Build systems, products and business practices on a security-by-design principle and industry best practice.

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Data Privacy by Design and Default
requirements.text: Build systems, products and business practices on a privacy-by-design principle, and set privacy options to protective defaults as the law requires.

mappings.rationale: Covers privacy and PII protection, but privacy by design and default are not explicit
Covers secure engineering principles, not privacy defaults

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Data Protection Impact Assessment
requirements.text: Carry out a data protection impact assessment to judge the origin, nature, particularities and severity of risks from processing personal data, as the law and good practice require.

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Sensitive Data Transfer
requirements.text: Any movement of personal or sensitive data must be safeguarded against unauthorised access, and the data may only be handled within the limits the applicable law sets.

mappings.rationale: Covers PII protection, but lawful scope of processing is not explicit

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Personal Data Access, Reversal, Rectification and Deletion
requirements.text: Let individuals ask to see, change or erase their personal data through supported processes and technical means, as the applicable law provides.

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Limitation of Purpose in Personal Data Processing
requirements.text: Personal data may be processed only in line with the law and for the purposes that were disclosed to the individual.

mappings.rationale: Covers privacy and PII protection, but purpose limitation is not explicit
Covers identifying legal requirements, not enforcing purpose limitation

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Personal Data Sub-processing
requirements.text: Control how personal data is handed on and sub-processed along the service supply chain, in line with applicable law.

mappings.rationale: Covers supplier relationships generally, not sub-processing of personal data
Covers PII protection, but sub-processing is not explicit

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Disclosure of Data Sub-processors
requirements.text: Tell the data owner, before processing starts, which sub-processors will access personal or sensitive data and how.

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Limitation of Production Data Use
requirements.text: Before production data is copied or used in non-production environments, the data owners must agree and the resulting risk must be handled.

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Data Retention and Deletion
requirements.text: Manage retention, archiving and deletion of data to fit business needs and applicable laws and regulations.

mappings.rationale: Covers protection and retention of records, not all data

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Sensitive Data Protection
requirements.text: Protect sensitive data through every stage of its lifecycle with suitable processes, procedures and technical measures.

mappings.rationale: Covers classification and handling, but not protection at every lifecycle stage
Covers data leakage prevention only

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Disclosure Notification
requirements.text: Providers must describe to customers, and apply, the procedure for handling law enforcement requests to disclose personal data, in line with applicable law.

requirements.section: Data Security and Privacy Lifecycle Management
requirements.title: Data Location
requirements.text: Document where data physically resides, including every location where it is handled or backed up.

requirements.title: Governance Program Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: An information governance programme backed by leadership should be underpinned by approved and communicated policies and procedures that are revisited yearly or after a material change.

mappings.rationale: Covers information security policy, not a wider governance programme

requirements.title: Risk Management Program
requirements.text: Run a documented enterprise-wide risk management programme with leadership backing; it should cover how risks are found, assessed, assigned to owners, treated and accepted.

mappings.rationale: Covers information security risk assessment, not enterprise-wide risk management
Covers information security risk treatment, not enterprise-wide risk management

requirements.title: Organizational Policy Reviews
requirements.text: Review all relevant organisational policies and their procedures yearly or whenever the organisation changes substantially.

requirements.title: Policy Exception Process
requirements.text: Follow an approved exception process, set by the governance programme, whenever something departs from an established policy.

requirements.title: Information Security Program
requirements.text: Run an information security programme spanning all CCM domains that apply.

requirements.title: Governance Responsibility Model
requirements.text: Define and record who is responsible for planning, running, assessing and improving governance programmes.

requirements.title: Information System Regulatory Mapping
requirements.text: List every standard, regulation and legal, contractual or statutory obligation that binds the organisation, and recheck the list at least annually or after a material change.

requirements.title: Special Interest Groups
requirements.text: Maintain relationships with cloud-focused interest groups and other bodies that matter given the organisation's business.

requirements.title: Background Screening Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Approved and communicated procedures should require background verification of every new hire, remote staff, contractors and third parties included, within local law, ethics and contract limits and in proportion to the data they will reach, business needs and acceptable risk. Revisit them yearly or after a material change.

requirements.title: Acceptable Use of Technology Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Approved and communicated procedures should state what use of organisation-owned or managed assets is allowed and on what conditions; revisit them yearly or after a material change.

requirements.title: Clean Desk Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Approved and communicated procedures should ensure unattended workspaces do not display confidential data openly; revisit them yearly or after a material change.

requirements.title: Remote and Home Working Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Approved policies and procedures should protect information that is accessed, handled or stored at remote or home-working sites; communicate them and revisit yearly or after a material change.

requirements.title: Asset returns
requirements.text: Write down how organisation-owned assets get returned when employees, contractors or third parties leave.

requirements.title: Employment Termination
requirements.text: Document and tell relevant personnel about the procedures that set out roles and responsibilities when employment changes or ends.

requirements.title: Employment Agreement Process
requirements.text: Have employees sign their employment agreement before they get access to systems, resources and assets.

requirements.title: Employment Agreement Content
requirements.text: Put terms in employment agreements requiring adherence to the established governance and security policies.

requirements.title: Personnel Roles and Responsibilities
requirements.text: Define, document and communicate employees' roles and responsibilities for the security and privacy of information assets.

requirements.title: Non-Disclosure Agreements
requirements.text: Identify, document and periodically review the need for non-disclosure or confidentiality agreements, reflecting how the organisation must protect data and operational details.

requirements.title: Security Awareness Training
requirements.text: Run a security awareness training programme for all employees, with regular refresher updates.

requirements.title: Personal and Sensitive Data Awareness and Training
requirements.text: Give staff who access sensitive organisational or personal data security training suited to their function, with regular updates on relevant policies and procedures.

requirements.title: Compliance User Responsibility
requirements.text: Make employees aware of their own part in complying with established policies and with applicable legal, statutory and regulatory obligations.

mappings.rationale: Covers awareness of policies, but not specifically of legal and regulatory duties

requirements.title: Identity and Access Management Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Identity and access management should be governed by approved policies and procedures that are communicated, put into practice and revisited yearly or after a material change.

requirements.title: Credentials Management Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Authentication credentials, passwords included, should be managed under approved policies and procedures that are communicated and put into practice and revisited yearly or after a material change.

requirements.title: Identity Inventory
requirements.text: Keep an inventory of identities, review it regularly and watch the access level each identity holds.

mappings.rationale: Covers review of access rights, but monitoring of identities' access level is not explicit

requirements.title: Separation of Duties
requirements.text: Apply separation of duties when granting access to information systems.

requirements.title: Least Privilege
requirements.text: Apply the least privilege principle when granting access to information systems.

requirements.title: Access Provisioning
requirements.text: Granting access should go through a process that approves each change to who can reach data and assets, records it and tells those affected.

requirements.title: Access Changes and Revocation
requirements.text: Remove or change identity access promptly when it is no longer appropriate.

requirements.title: Access Review
requirements.text: Access should be rechecked for least privilege and separation of duties as often as the organisation's risk tolerance demands, no less than once a year, and after major changes.

requirements.title: Segregation of Privileged Access Roles
requirements.text: Keep privileged access roles apart from each other through suitable processes, procedures and technical measures.

mappings.rationale: Covers separation of conflicting duties generally
Covers privileged access rights, but segregating privileged roles is not explicit

requirements.title: Management of Privileged Access Roles
requirements.text: Grant privileged roles and rights only for a limited time and prevent the build-up of privileged roles that should stay separate.

mappings.rationale: Privileged rights are allocated in a controlled way, but time-limited grants and preventing accumulation are not explicit

requirements.title: Service Customers Approval for Agreed Privileged Access Roles
requirements.text: Let customers take part, where relevant, in granting agreed high-risk privileged access roles that the provider's staff hold.

requirements.title: Unique Identities
requirements.text: Each identity needs its own unique ID so that its activity can be attributed.

requirements.title: Strong Authentication
requirements.text: Access to systems, applications and data must be authenticated. Least-privileged users and sensitive data access require multiple factors, and system identities should use digital certificates or something equally strong.

mappings.rationale: Secure authentication is required, but multifactor authentication and certificates for system identities are not mandated

requirements.title: Credentials Management
requirements.text: Authentication credentials, passwords included, must be handled securely.

requirements.title: Authorization Mechanisms
requirements.text: Check that every access to data and system functions has been authorised.

requirements.title: Interoperability and Portability Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Approved, communicated policies and procedures should address interoperability and portability: how application interfaces communicate, how information processing interoperates, how application development stays portable, and how data is exchanged, used, ported, kept intact and persisted. Revisit them yearly or after a material change.

mappings.rationale: Covers data portability, but interface interoperability and application development portability are not included

requirements.title: Application Interface Availability
requirements.text: Offer customers application interfaces through which they can retrieve their data programmatically, supporting interoperability and portability.

requirements.title: Secure Interoperability and Portability Management
requirements.text: Use cryptographically secure network protocols that follow industry standards to manage, import and export data.

mappings.rationale: Covers use of cryptography, but secure protocols for data import and export are not explicit
Covers secure information transfer in general

requirements.title: Data Portability Contractual Obligations
requirements.text: Include contract terms stating customers' access to their data after termination: the data format, how long data is kept, what data is retained and made available, and the deletion policy.

mappings.rationale: Covers security terms in supplier agreements, not data return on termination

requirements.title: Infrastructure and Virtualization Security Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Infrastructure and virtualisation security should be governed by approved policies and procedures that are communicated and revisited yearly or after a material change.

mappings.rationale: Covers network security, but infrastructure and virtualisation policy is not explicit
Covers configuration management, not a dedicated infrastructure policy

requirements.title: Capacity and Resource Planning
requirements.text: Resource availability, quality and capacity should be planned and watched so that systems perform as the business requires.

requirements.title: Network Security
requirements.text: Traffic between environments, services and applications should be watched, encrypted and limited to authenticated and authorised connections with a business reason. Each allowed service, protocol and port needs a written justification (and any compensating controls), and the configuration is reviewed at least once a year.

mappings.rationale: Covers separating network groups, but not documented justification for every allowed flow

requirements.title: OS Hardening and Base Controls
requirements.text: Secure the hosts, guest systems, hypervisors and infrastructure control plane through hardening that follows their vendors' and the industry's best practices, enforced technically and kept as part of a security baseline.

requirements.title: Production and Non-Production Environments
requirements.text: Keep production and non-production environments apart so production data is not used in non-production, and sanitise or protect production data before any authorised use there.

requirements.title: Segmentation and Segregation
requirements.text: Build and configure applications and infrastructure so that each customer's (tenant's) access is properly segmented, segregated, monitored and restricted.

mappings.rationale: Covers segregation of networks, not tenant isolation in shared platforms

requirements.title: Migration to Cloud Environments
requirements.text: Migrations of servers, services, applications or data into the cloud should travel over protected, encrypted channels that rely solely on current and approved protocols.

mappings.rationale: Covers secure information transfer, but migration to cloud is not explicit
Covers use of cryptography, but approved protocols for migration are not explicit

requirements.title: Network Architecture Documentation
requirements.text: Work out which environments carry elevated risk, judged by how sensitive their data is, how exposed they are to threats and what a failure would cost the business, and write this down.

mappings.rationale: Covers separation of networks, but identifying and documenting high-risk environments is not explicit
Covers risk assessment generally, not environment documentation

requirements.title: Network Defense
requirements.text: Apply defence-in-depth techniques to protect against, detect and quickly respond to network-based attacks.

mappings.rationale: Covers network protection, but defence-in-depth is not explicit
Covers monitoring for anomalous behaviour, but response to network attacks is not explicit

requirements.title: Logging and Monitoring Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Logging and monitoring should be governed by an approved policy and procedure set, communicated to staff and revisited yearly or after a material change.

mappings.rationale: Covers logging, but a dedicated policy is not required
Covers monitoring activities, but a dedicated policy is not required

requirements.title: Audit Logs Protection
requirements.text: Ensure audit logs are kept securely and retained for as long as needed.

requirements.title: Security Monitoring and Alerting
requirements.text: Identify and monitor security events in applications and the infrastructure beneath them, and generate alerts to the responsible people based on those events and related metrics.

requirements.title: Audit Logs Access and Accountability
requirements.text: Limit audit log access to authorised identities and keep records of that access.

requirements.title: Audit Logs Monitoring and Response
requirements.text: Correlate and watch security audit logs so unusual or suspicious activity stands out from normal patterns, and have a defined routine for reviewing and acting on such findings promptly.

requirements.title: Clock Synchronization
requirements.text: All relevant systems that process information should take their clock from one trustworthy source.

requirements.title: Logging Scope
requirements.text: Decide, document and implement which system events and metadata are logged, and revisit the scope yearly, when the threat environment changes and as regulation requires.

requirements.title: Audit Logs Sanitization
requirements.text: Give customers technical means to find and remove or tokenise sensitive data in logs, to prevent unauthorised exposure as the law requires.

mappings.rationale: Covers data masking, but customer-facing detection and scrubbing of logs is not explicit
Covers protection of log information, but not scrubbing sensitive data from it

requirements.title: Log Records
requirements.text: Produce audit records that contain the relevant security information.

requirements.title: Audit Records Protection
requirements.text: Protect audit records from unauthorised access, change and deletion.

requirements.title: Encryption Monitoring and Reporting
requirements.text: Be able to observe, and report to management, how cryptography and key management are actually run: the policies, processes, procedures and controls around them.

mappings.rationale: Covers monitoring activities, but cryptography-specific monitoring is not explicit

requirements.title: Transaction/Activity Logging
requirements.text: Log and monitor key lifecycle events so that key usage can be audited and reported.

mappings.rationale: Covers logging of activities, but key lifecycle events are not explicit

requirements.title: Access Control Logs
requirements.text: Monitor and log physical access with an access control system that can be audited.

mappings.rationale: Covers physical monitoring, but auditable access logs are not explicit

requirements.title: Failures and Anomalies Reporting
requirements.text: Report failures and anomalies of the monitoring system itself, with immediate notice to the accountable party.

mappings.rationale: Covers monitoring, but failures of the monitoring system and immediate notification are not explicit

requirements.section: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, & Cloud Forensics
requirements.title: Security Incident Management Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: A reviewed and approved policy set, communicated to staff, should govern security incident handling together with e-discovery and cloud forensic work, and be revisited annually or when circumstances shift materially.

mappings.rationale: Covers evidence collection, but e-discovery and cloud forensics are not explicit

requirements.section: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, & Cloud Forensics
requirements.title: Service Management Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Approved and communicated policies and procedures should govern timely handling of security incidents; revisit them yearly or after a material change.

requirements.section: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, & Cloud Forensics
requirements.title: Incident Response Plans
requirements.text: Keep an approved incident response plan; among other things it should lay out how internal teams, affected customers and other dependent parties such as supply chain partners are told about an incident.

requirements.section: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, & Cloud Forensics
requirements.title: Incident Response Testing
requirements.text: Rehearse the incident response plans on a planned schedule and after material change.

mappings.rationale: Covers incident planning and preparation, but exercising the plans is not explicit

requirements.section: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, & Cloud Forensics
requirements.title: Incident Response Metrics
requirements.text: Set up measures of information security incidents, track them and report on them.

mappings.rationale: Covers performance measurement generally, not incident metrics

requirements.section: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, & Cloud Forensics
requirements.title: Event Triage Processes
requirements.text: Support business processes with processes and technical measures that triage security-related events.

requirements.section: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, & Cloud Forensics
requirements.title: Incident Management and Response
requirements.text: Respond to security incidents promptly and effectively according to incident category and severity, and review, update and test the procedures at least yearly.

requirements.section: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, & Cloud Forensics
requirements.title: Security Breach Notification

mappings.rationale: Covers response to incidents, but breach notification duties are not explicit

requirements.section: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, & Cloud Forensics
requirements.title: Incident Records Management
requirements.text: Keep a secure repository of incident records and review it regularly to spot patterns, root causes and systemic weaknesses, then correct them.

requirements.section: Security Incident Management, E-Discovery, & Cloud Forensics
requirements.title: Points of Contact Maintenance
requirements.text: Keep current contact details for regulators, police at national and local level and other authorities with jurisdiction, and refresh them at least annually.

requirements.section: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
requirements.title: Supply Chain Risk Management Policies and Procedures
requirements.text: Supply chain risk management should be governed by an approved policy and procedure set, communicated to staff and revisited yearly or after a material change.

requirements.section: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
requirements.title: SSRM Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Application of the shared security responsibility model inside the organisation should be governed by approved and communicated policies and procedures, revisited yearly or after a material change.

mappings.rationale: Covers use of cloud services, but not the provider's own shared responsibility policy

requirements.section: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
requirements.title: SSRM Supply Chain
requirements.text: Apply, record and manage the shared security responsibility model throughout the supply chain.

mappings.rationale: Covers the ICT supply chain generally, not the shared responsibility model

requirements.section: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
requirements.title: SSRM Guidance
requirements.text: Give customers guidance explaining how the shared security responsibility model applies across the supply chain.

requirements.section: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
requirements.title: SSRM Control Ownership
requirements.text: Spell out which party owns each CCM control and where it applies under the shared security responsibility model.

requirements.section: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
requirements.title: SSRM Documentation Review
requirements.text: Review and validate the shared security responsibility documentation.

requirements.section: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
requirements.title: SSRM Control Implementation

requirements.section: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability

requirements.section: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
requirements.title: Service Bill of Material (BOM)
requirements.text: Define and enforce a process to build a bill of materials for the service supply chain, and review it yearly or after significant change.

requirements.section: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
requirements.title: Supply Chain Risk Management
requirements.text: Review the risk factors tied to supply chain relationships at regular intervals.

requirements.section: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
requirements.title: Primary Service and Contractual Agreement
requirements.text: Include in service agreements mutually agreed terms on: scope, characteristics and location of services; security requirements including the shared responsibility model; change management; logging and monitoring; incident handling and communication; audit rights; termination; interoperability and portability; data privacy; and operational resilience.

requirements.section: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
requirements.title: Supply Chain Agreement Review
requirements.text: Review supply chain agreements yearly or after significant change.

requirements.section: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability
requirements.title: Supply Chain Compliance Assessment
requirements.text: At least once a year, run internal assessments checking whether standards, policies, procedures and service level activities are conformed to and working.

mappings.rationale: Covers compliance reviews, but supply chain assessments are not explicit

requirements.section: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability

requirements.text: Adopt policies obliging each provider in the supply chain to honour the organisation's expectations on security, confidentiality, access control, privacy, audit, staffing and service levels.

requirements.section: Supply Chain Management, Transparency, and Accountability

requirements.title: Threat and Vulnerability Management Policy and Procedures

requirements.title: Malware and Malicious Instructions Protection Policy and Procedures
requirements.text: Protection from malware and malicious instructions should be governed by approved and communicated policies and procedures, revisited yearly or after a material change.

requirements.title: Vulnerability Identification

mappings.rationale: Covers technical vulnerability management, but a monthly detection cadence is not required

requirements.title: Threat Analysis and Modelling

mappings.rationale: Covers threat intelligence, but threat modelling is not explicit

requirements.title: Vulnerability Remediation Schedule

requirements.title: Threat Response

requirements.title: Vulnerability Management Reporting

requirements.title: Vulnerability Management Metrics
